summary:
H.R. 7266, the "Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act," amends Section 40124 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (42 U.S.C. 18723) by striking it and substituting a revised text that reauthorizes and modifies the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program administered by the Secretary (of Energy). The operative mechanism is a complete restatement of Section 40124 rather than a discrete series of amendments.

The revised Section 40124(a) provides definitions, incorporating by cross-reference the meanings of "bulk-power system" (section 215(a), Federal Power Act), "cybersecurity threat" (section 2200, Homeland Security Act of 2002), and "defense critical electric infrastructure" (section 215A(a), Federal Power Act). "Eligible entity" is defined to include rural electric cooperatives; municipally or other politically subdivided publicly owned utilities; utilities owned by an agency, authority, corporation, or instrumentality of one or more political subdivisions; a not-for-profit entity partnered with at least six such entities; and investor-owned utilities selling fewer than 4,000,000 megawatt hours annually.

Subsection (b) directs the Secretary to "maintain" the Program (rather than merely establish it), providing technical assistance and funding—including grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes—to protect against, detect, respond to, and recover from cybersecurity threats. Subsection (c) states the Program's objectives: deployment of advanced cybersecurity technologies and increased participation in cybersecurity threat information-sharing programs.

Subsection (d) requires the Secretary, subject to the availability of appropriations, to provide assistance and award funding on a competitive or noncompetitive basis; to develop award criteria; and to establish a process to inform eligible entities of opportunities. It permits ("may") the Secretary to enter facilitating agreements. Subsection (d)(2) mandates funding priority for eligible entities that, as the Secretary determines, have limited cybersecurity resources, own assets critical to bulk-power system reliability, or own or operate defense critical electric infrastructure.

Subsection (e) provides that information shared by or with the Federal Government or a State, Tribal, or local government under the Program is deemed voluntarily shared and exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552) and analogous State, Tribal, or local open-government, open-meetings, open-records, or sunshine laws.

Subsection (f) authorizes appropriations of $250,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2026 through 2030. This is an authorization of appropriations, not an appropriation; disbursement of funding under subsection (d) is expressly conditioned on the availability of appropriations.

The bill contains no separate effective-date provision; the amendment takes effect upon enactment. The measure was reported to the House (Report No. 119-629) and placed on the Union Calendar (No. 545).
